record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: For κ > 1, let pκ be the minimal size of a centered family in [N]^{ℵ0} that cannot be partitioned into fewer than κ subfamilies each with a pseudo-intersection. Is p_p equal to t?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the Boolean algebra P(ℕ)/fin. A family F ⊆ [ℕ]^{ℵ₀} is called centered if every finite subfamily of F has infinite intersection. A pseudo-intersection of a family F ⊆ [ℕ]^{ℵ₀} is a set A ∈ [ℕ]^{ℵ₀} such that A ⊆* B (i.e. A∖B is finite) for every B ∈ F.

The classical pseudo-intersection number p is the minimum cardinality of a centered family in [ℕ]^{ℵ₀} that has no pseudo-intersection. The tower number t is the minimum cardinality of a ⊆*-decreasing chain in [ℕ]^{ℵ₀} that has no pseudo-intersection.

For a cardinal κ > 1, define
  p_κ = min{ |F| : F ⊆ [ℕ]^{ℵ₀} is centered and F cannot be partitioned into fewer than κ subfamilies, each of which has a pseudo-intersection }.

(So p_2 = p.)

Question: Is p_p = t?
artifact.status_search_result: Malliaris and Shelah proved p = t in ZFC (2012/2013), which resolves the classical equality but does not by itself answer whether the partition-refinement variant p_p equals t = p. Web searches did not surface a definitive resolution of the specific question p_p = t in the literature on selection principles or cardinal characteristics; its status appears unclear.

status_evidence.title: General topology meets model theory, on p and t
status_evidence.snippet: Malliaris and Shelah prove p = t in ZFC.
status_evidence.claim: p = t is a theorem of ZFC, but this does not directly settle p_p = t.

status_evidence.title: Selection Principles and special sets of reals: Open problems
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems including the hierarchy between p and t.
status_evidence.claim: The problem p_p = t is posed as part of a hierarchy between p and t.
